questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator would like to minimize stale CIs in the CMDB.
Which CMDB Health Dashboard scorecard displays this information?

options.text: Correctness
Compliance
Completeness

questions.explanation: The Correctness scorecard on the CMDB Health Dashboard tracks stale CIs. Correctness is a KPI that aggregates three metrics: Orphan, Staleness, and Duplicate. The Staleness metric measures the percentage of CIs not updated within a configured duration (default 60 days). Since the administrator wants to minimize stale CIs, the Correctness scorecard (A) is where this information is displayed. Compliance tracks adherence to rules, and Completeness tracks missing/empty CI attributes — neither directly addresses staleness.

questions.stem:
DRAG DROP -
Drag and drop the application service type to the best description.
questions.explanation: Service Mapping (Top-down) - Recommended for mission-critical application services that require a precise approach using patterns; Tag-Based - Best fit to map cloud-native container-based or virtual machine environments; Service Mapping (Connection Suggestion) - Ideal for custom-built applications and leverages application fingerprinting to generate service maps in a timely manner; Dynamic CI Group - Ideal for small application services that can be easily grouped using filters and CMDB queries. The answer image shows the correct drag-and-drop mapping: Service Mapping (Top-down) uses patterns for precise, mission-critical service mapping. Tag-Based mapping is designed for cloud-native, container, and VM environments where tags identify relationships. Service Mapping (Connection Suggestion) uses application fingerprinting to quickly generate service maps for custom-built applications. Dynamic CI Group is for small application services that can be grouped using CMDB queries and filters without complex mapping patterns.

questions.stem:
A new custom class is needed to reflect a new application being managed in the CMDB.
Which roles are minimally needed to add this custom CI class?

options.text: A cmdb_inst_admin and personalize_form
itil_admin and personalize_form
data_classification_admin and personalize_dictionary
sn_cmdb_admin and personalize_dictionary

questions.explanation: Creating a custom CI class requires two capabilities: managing CMDB classes and creating new table structures. sn_cmdb_admin provides CMDB administration rights to create/manage CI classes, and personalize_dictionary allows creating new fields and tables (dictionary entries). Option A (cmdb_inst_admin) doesn't grant class creation rights. Option B (itil_admin) lacks CMDB class management permissions. Option C (data_classification_admin) is for data classification, not class management. personalize_form (in A and B) only allows layout changes, not the dictionary-level changes needed for new classes.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between an application and a server?

options.text: Application>Used by::Uses>Server
Application> Uses::Used by>Server
Application>Runs::Runs On>Server
Application>Runs on::Runs>Server

questions.explanation: CMDB relationship types use the format Parent>Relationship::Reverse Relationship>Child. An application 'Runs on' a server, meaning from the application's perspective the relationship is 'Runs on', and from the server's perspective 'Runs'. The correct notation is Application>Runs on::Runs>Server (D). Option C reverses the direction incorrectly (Application>Runs would mean the server runs on the application). Options A and B use 'Uses/Used by' which describes a different dependency type, not an execution hosting relationship.

questions.stem:
User endpoint devices are imported into the CMDB and populate the ‘Assigned to’ [assigned_to] field on the Computer [cmdb_ci_computer] CI. The Asset team puts in a request for the Configuration Analysts to populate the ‘Assigned to’ field on the related Asset.
What action does a Configuration Analyst take to achieve this in an automated way?

options.text: Use the Asset-CI Field Mapping module to create a new rule to replicate the ‘Assigned to’ value between the asset and associated CI
Hide the ‘Assigned to’ field on the asset record and create a new field that dot walks to the related CI to get the ‘Assigned to’ value
Configure a business rule on the computer table to use a script to populate the ‘Assigned to’ filed on the asset based on insert or update in the computer class ‘Assigned to’ field

questions.explanation: The Asset-CI Field Mapping module creates rules to automatically replicate field values between assets and their associated CIs. By creating a mapping rule for the 'Assigned to' field, when the CI's 'Assigned to' is populated, the related Asset's field is automatically updated. This is the proper automated approach. Hiding the field with dot-walking (B) is a workaround, and a custom business rule (C) is unnecessarily complex.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator needs to create a new CI class for the Internet of Things (IoT) Sensor in ServiceNow.
What are the recommended practices for this specific activity? (Choose two.)

options.text: Add a new class under an appropriate parent class
Modify an existing class
Install or update the CMDB CI Class Models store application, and verify the class does not already exist
Delete an unused class, and replace it with the new one

questions.explanation: When creating a new CI class, recommended practices are: (A) add the new class under an appropriate parent class in the hierarchy, and (C) install or update the CMDB CI Class Models store application first to verify the class doesn't already exist. Modifying an existing class (B) defeats the purpose of creating a new class. Deleting an unused class to replace it (D) is destructive and not recommended.

questions.stem:
A Change Manager aims to streamline ITSM processes by automatically populating fields on the Change form when a CI is selected. The Configuration Management team is working to ensure that the Change Group field is populated for all managed CIs.
As a result, which base system field on the incident form will be automatically populated after selecting a CI?

options.text: Managed by group
Approval group
Assignment group
Change group

questions.explanation: When a CI is selected on an incident form, the Assignment group field is automatically populated from the CI's Support group. This is a base system behavior that routes incidents to the team responsible for supporting that CI. Managed by group (A) is tracked on the CI for governance but doesn't auto-populate on incidents. Approval group (B) and Change group (D) serve different ITSM functions.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow solution creates automatic relationships?

options.text: IntegrationHub ETL
Discovery
Workflow Studio
Service Mapping

questions.explanation: Discovery automatically creates CIs and the relationships between them in the CMDB. When Discovery runs, it scans networks and infrastructure, identifying hardware, software, and their dependencies, then populates both CI records and their relationships automatically. IntegrationHub ETL (A) imports data but doesn't auto-discover relationships. Workflow Studio (C) is for building workflows, not CI discovery. Service Mapping (D) maps application services to infrastructure but Discovery is the core solution specifically described as creating 'automatic relationships.'

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator is reviewing the health of the CMDB and notices a large percentage of the Hardware CIs are missing serial numbers. The Administrator is concerned this may cause duplicate CIs and would like to resolve the issue in a timely manner.
What structured guidelines provided by ServiceNow are available to troubleshoot and resolve the issue?

options.text: CMDB Health Dashboards Playbooks
CSDM Now Create Playbooks
CSDB Data Foundations Dashboard Playbooks
CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard Playbooks

questions.explanation: The CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard Playbooks (CSDB is the abbreviation used in option C) provide structured guidelines for troubleshooting CMDB health issues like missing serial numbers. Option A ('CMDB Health Dashboards Playbooks') is not an official product name. Option D references CSDM (Common Service Data Model), which is about data model frameworks, not CI data quality troubleshooting. Option B ('CSDM Now Create Playbooks') relates to framework content setup, not quality remediation.

questions.stem:
Configuration Management needs to ensure data quality for all CIs in the CMDB.
What areas of data quality for CIs are in the CMDB Health Dashboard? (Choose two.)

options.text: Missing CIs
State CIs
Duplicate CIs
Downgraded CIs
Upgraded CIs

questions.explanation: The CMDB Health Dashboard evaluates data quality through three KPIs: Correctness, Completeness, and Compliance. Under Correctness, the metrics are Orphan, Staleness (Stale CIs), and Duplicate (Duplicate CIs). Option B ('State CIs' likely refers to 'Stale CIs') and C (Duplicate CIs) match the Staleness and Duplicate metrics under the Correctness KPI. Missing CIs (A), Downgraded CIs (D), and Upgraded CIs (E) are not metrics tracked by the CMDB Health Dashboard.

questions.stem:
The CMDB Configuration Management team has successfully developed a healthy and trusted CMDB. They have integrated discovered infrastructure data, accurately referenced non-discoverable data (such as change and support group information), and made the CMDB service-aware using Service Mapping.
Which field on an Incident form is automatically populated after a CI is selected that references an appropriate support group?

options.text: Support Group
Approval Group
Change Group
Assignment Group
Managed by Group

questions.explanation: When a CI with an appropriate support group is selected on an Incident form, the Assignment Group field is automatically populated. The support group defined on the CI maps to the incident's Assignment Group, routing the incident to the correct team. Support Group (A) appears on the CI but isn't a field populated on the incident form. Approval Group (B), Change Group (C), and Managed by Group (E) serve different purposes.

questions.stem:
CMDB class owners are receiving tasks under the ‘My Work’ tab in the CMDB Workspace.
Which CMDB management tool is generating these tasks?

options.text: CMDB Data Manager
De-duplication templates
CMDB Health Dashboard

questions.explanation: CMDB Data Manager generates attestation, certification, and lifecycle tasks for CMDB class owners. These tasks appear under the 'My Work' tab in CMDB Workspace, where owners can review, attest, approve, reject, or reassign CIs. De-duplication templates (B) help merge duplicate CIs but don't generate tasks under My Work. The CMDB Health Dashboard (C) displays health metrics and scorecards but doesn't create tasks for class owners.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator wants only the CIs of Principal Classes to appear in CI reference fields, for example the CI reference fields accessible from an Incident Form.
Where does the CMDB Administrator designate Principal Classes?

options.text: CI Class Manager
CMDB Workspace
CMDB Data Manager
System Properties

questions.explanation: Principal Classes are designated in the CI Class Manager. This tool allows administrators to view, create, and edit class definitions including marking classes as 'Principal'. When a class is marked as Principal, only CIs of those classes appear in CI reference fields (e.g., on an Incident form). CMDB Workspace (B) is for monitoring health, Data Manager (C) is for policies, and System Properties (D) doesn't manage class designations.

questions.stem:
The following Reconciliation Rules were configured for ServiceNow, Altiris, and SCCM:

Which are true? (Choose two.)

options.text: Data collected with a discovery source of SCCM can update any record in the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table because it has the highest priority number.
Data collected with a discovery source of ServiceNow can insert new records into the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table, but cannot update records created by Altiris or SCCM.
Data collected with a discovery source of Altiris can update records inserted by SCCM into the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table.
Data collected with a discovery source of SCCM can be inserted as new records in the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table.

questions.explanation: The image shows Reconciliation Rules: ServiceNow priority=100 (highest precedence), Altiris=200, SCCM=300 (lowest precedence). Lower priority number means higher precedence. (C) Altiris (200) can update SCCM (300) records because Altiris has higher precedence. (D) SCCM can insert new records — all authorized sources can create new CIs regardless of priority. (A) is wrong — SCCM has the LOWEST precedence despite the highest number, so it cannot update others' records. (B) is wrong — ServiceNow has the HIGHEST precedence and can update any record.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator needs to import external data into the CMDB. As the CMDB Administrator wants to reduce the risk for creating duplicates and to update information from unauthorized sources, it has to be ensured that the Identification and Reconciliation API will not be bypassed.
What is the recommended method to import data into the CMDB utilizing the Identification and Reconciliation API?

options.text: IntegrationHub ETL
Table API (REST API or SOAP API)
Import Sets and Transform Maps

questions.explanation: IntegrationHub ETL natively uses the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) when importing data into the CMDB, ensuring CIs are properly identified and reconciled. Import Sets with Transform Maps (C) can use IRE but only if configured with onAfter scripts, making it easier to accidentally bypass. Table API (B) also doesn't inherently go through IRE. IntegrationHub ETL is the recommended approach for IRE-compliant data imports.

questions.stem:
A Configuration Manager has configured a multiple data sources which are all authorized to update the same class and the same set of class attributes in the CMDB.
What can the Configuration Manager do to control which data source should be authoritative source of truth for a specific class of set of class attributes?

options.text: Assign a priority to each data source in the reconciliation rules
Manually run the data source updates in the correct order
Configure data refresh rules with a specific time period
Assign a run order to each data source in the identification rules

questions.explanation: Reconciliation rules control which discovery source is authoritative for specific classes and attributes. By assigning a priority to each data source in the reconciliation rules, you establish which source takes precedence when multiple are authorized to update the same attributes. Higher priority sources can overwrite lower priority ones, but not vice versa (unless the CI attribute is stale). This is the standard mechanism for managing data source authority.

questions.stem:
Which CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB the Dynamic Reconciliation Rules will also be enabled. Based on the request of the management, a CMDB Administrator has to set up multiple Dynamic Reconciliation Rules.
Which are available ‘Dynamic Rule Types’ within the ‘Create Reconciliation Rule’ wizard? (Choose two.)

options.text: Last Updated
Smallest Value
Last Created
Most Reported

questions.explanation: Dynamic Reconciliation Rules in CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB support two rule types: 'Last Updated' (most recently updated value wins) and 'Most Reported' (value reported by the majority of discovery sources wins). 'Smallest Value' (B) and 'Last Created' (C) are not available dynamic rule types. Dynamic rules take precedence over static reconciliation rules for the same CI attribute.

questions.stem:
The following identification rule for a CI class has been defined:
Two new CI records are imported into the hardware class of the CMDB:
CI1: The name of this CI record matches the name of an existing CI record in the CMDB.
CI2: The IP address of this CI record matches the IP address of an existing CI record in the CMDB.
Which is correct based on the identification rule and the imported CI records?

options.text: CI1 will be inserted as new record and CI2 will be updated with matching record.
CI1 will be updated with matching record and CI2 will be inserted as new record.
CI1 and CI2 both will be updated with matching records.
CI1 and CI2 both will be inserted as new records.

questions.explanation: When an identification rule has criterion attributes (name AND IP address) in a single identifier entry, ALL criteria must match for a CI to be identified. CI1 matches only the name and CI2 matches only the IP address, but neither matches BOTH criteria simultaneously. Since no complete match is found for either, both are inserted as new records in the CMDB rather than being matched to existing CIs.

questions.stem:
A customer wants recently imported server records to be automatically reclassified into more specific CMDB classes after being discovered using ServiceNow Discovery.
During the discovery process, if existing Server [cmdb_ci_server] records are reclassified into the Linux [cmdb_ci_linux_server] and Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] classes, which reclassification operation occurred?

options.text: Class Upgrade
Class Downgrade
Class Switch

questions.explanation: When Discovery reclassifies a CI from a parent class (Server) to a more specific child class (Linux Server or Windows Server), this is a Class Upgrade. The CI moves down the class hierarchy to a more specific subclass. Class Downgrade (B) would be moving from a more specific to a more general class. Class Switch (C) would involve moving to a sibling class at the same level. Server to Linux/Windows Server is always an upgrade.

questions.stem:
A Platform Data Owner wants to improve data quality with a few reconciliation rules across the five discovery sources that are being used. The Data Owner knows the best option is to include CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB to manage and monitor discovery sources, but the company currently does not have a license for ITOM Discovery that is required for CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB.
What can the Data Owner do in this case?

options.text: ITOM Discovery needs to be purchased to take advantage of the multisource IRE Rules.
CMBD 360/Multisource is a platform product that can be used immediately.
The IRE reconciliation rules can use discovery source regardless of CMDB 360 being enabled.

questions.explanation: IRE reconciliation rules can use discovery source regardless of whether CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB is enabled. Reconciliation rules with discovery source-based prioritization are a core IRE feature available on all CMDB installations. CMDB 360 adds enhanced multi-source management (dynamic rules, coverage views) but is not required for basic reconciliation rule functionality. No additional licensing is needed for standard reconciliation.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow solution creates automatic relationships?

options.text: IntegrationHub ETL
Discovery
Workflow Studio
Service Mapping

questions.explanation: Service Mapping automatically creates relationships between CIs by tracing connections from entry points through the infrastructure. Unlike manual CMDB updates or Discovery (which primarily finds individual CIs), Service Mapping specifically maps dependencies and creates relationship records between application services and their underlying infrastructure components.

questions.stem:
The Apache Web Server Identification Rule is configured with the following Criterion attributes:
Class -
Configuration file -
Version -
Yesterday, an Apache Web Server CI was discovered as part of Service Mapping. Today, the application owner upgraded Apache to a different version and reran discovery of the service.
What will happen in the CMDB?

options.text: The existing Apache Web Server CI will be reconciled and its version will be updated.
A duplication error will occur.
The Apache Web Server CI will be reclassified as a Web Server CI.
A new Apache Web Server CI is created.

questions.explanation: The Apache Web Server identification rule uses Class, Configuration file, and Version as criterion attributes. When the version changes after an upgrade, the new discovery data no longer matches the existing CI on ALL criteria (the version is different). Since identification requires all criterion attributes to match, the IRE treats the new data as a different CI and creates a new Apache Web Server CI record in the CMDB.

questions.stem:
Configuration Management requires an accurate inventory of devices to be reflected in the CMDB.
Which are common use cases for using Agent Client Collector (ACC)? (Choose two.)

options.text: Network devices in the DMZ
Devices that intermittently connect to the network
Servers in the data center
Devices in secure environments

questions.explanation: Agent Client Collector (ACC) is ideal for: (B) devices that intermittently connect to the network — ACC runs locally and reports when connectivity is available, and (D) devices in secure environments where agentless discovery cannot reach. Network devices in the DMZ (A) are better discovered via SNMP/network-based discovery. Data center servers (C) are typically discovered by standard agentless Discovery.

questions.stem:
An organization needs to maintain non-discoverable attributes, such as warranty expiration dates, for hardware CIs. These attributes are not updated by automated discovery tools.
What method ensures these attributes are accurately maintained for all CIs?

options.text: Create a new CI class specifically for non-discoverable attributes
Use the CMDB Reconciliation Engine to update the attributes
Use a scheduled data import to update the attributes from an external source

questions.explanation: For non-discoverable attributes like warranty expiration dates, a scheduled data import from an external source (such as a vendor database or spreadsheet) ensures these attributes are accurately maintained. Creating a new CI class (A) doesn't solve the attribute update problem. The CMDB Reconciliation Engine (B) handles data from discovery sources but doesn't inherently source non-discoverable attributes.

questions.stem:
DRAG DROP -
ServiceNow provides a suite of CMDB management tools designed to effectively ingest, manage, and maintain CIs and relationships.
Drag and drop the design architecture to its management tool.
Some options may not apply.
questions.explanation: CMDB management tools include: CI Class Manager (manages class hierarchy, identification rules, health settings), CMDB Data Manager (governs CI lifecycle with policies), CMDB Health Dashboard (monitors CMDB quality metrics), and CMDB Query Builder (queries CI relationships). Each tool has a specific design architecture for ingesting, managing, and maintaining CIs and relationships.

questions.stem: When integrating data into the CMDB using import sets and transform maps, which type of script is added to ensure the data is processed through the IRE?

options.text: onBefore
onComplete
onStart
onAfter

questions.explanation: The onAfter script is added to transform maps to ensure data passes through the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE). The onAfter script executes after data rows are transformed and inserted, calling the IRE API to process the imported CIs for proper identification, reconciliation, and de-duplication. onBefore (A) runs before transformation, onComplete (B) runs after all rows, and onStart (C) runs at the beginning of the import.

questions.stem: The following Reconciliation Rules were configured for ServiceNow, Altiris, and SCCM: Which are true? (Choose two.)

options.text: Data collected with a discovery source of SCCM can update any record in the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table because it has the highest priority number.
Data collected with a discovery source of ServiceNow can insert new records into the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table, but cannot update records created by Altiris or SCCM.
Data collected with a discovery source of Altiris can update records inserted by SCCM into the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table.
Data collected with a discovery source of SCCM can be inserted as new records in the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table.

questions.explanation: When reconciliation rules with different priorities exist, the source with the higher priority number takes precedence. After an authorized discovery source updates an attribute, subsequent updates are accepted only from the same or higher priority source. A lower-priority source cannot overwrite values set by a higher-priority one, ensuring data integrity from the most authoritative sources.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator has installed a Service Graph Connector and customized a script transform.
What will happen on subsequent upgrades if the default definition of the script transform is updated?

options.text: A skipped change is created and no change is made the script transform definition.
The Service Graph Connector upgrade refuses to start.
The upgrade stops and reports an error.

questions.explanation: When a Service Graph Connector is upgraded and the default script transform definition has been updated, but you've customized it, a 'skipped change' record is created. The upgrade does not overwrite your customization — instead it logs the skipped change so you can review the new default and manually merge changes if needed. The upgrade neither refuses to start (B) nor stops with an error (C).

questions.stem: A CMDB Administrator would like to minimize stale CIs in the CMDB. Which CMDB Health Dashboard scorecard displays this information?

options.text: Correctness
Compliance
Completeness

questions.explanation: The Correctness scorecard on the CMDB Health Dashboard tracks stale CIs. Correctness is a KPI that aggregates three metrics: Orphan (CIs with no relationships), Staleness (CIs not updated within a specified duration, default 60 days), and Duplicate (redundant CI records). To minimize stale CIs, the administrator should review the Correctness scorecard's Staleness metric.

questions.stem:
DRAG DROP -
Drag and drop the CMDB Health Dashboard metric to the description.
questions.explanation: CMDB Health Dashboard metrics under Correctness: Orphan (CIs with no relationships or missing data), Staleness (CIs not updated within the effective duration, default 60 days), Duplicate (CIs matching identification criteria). Under Completeness: Required Fields (missing mandatory attributes), Recommended Fields. Under Compliance: based on audit run results.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator is asked to clean up the CMDB duplicates.
What is the preferred way to manage this task?

options.text: My Tasks in the Application Navigator
The de-duplication task module
The de-duplication dashboard on the CMDB workspace

questions.explanation: The de-duplication dashboard on the CMDB Workspace provides a comprehensive view for managing CMDB duplicates, including identifying, reviewing, and merging duplicate CIs. While the de-duplication task module (B) exists, the dashboard in CMDB Workspace is the preferred modern approach. My Tasks in the Application Navigator (A) shows assigned tasks but isn't the primary duplicate management tool.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator identifies duplicate CIs. One was created by a manual import, and the other one was created by automated discovery. The discovered CI has the latest IP address, while the manually imported CI has an accurate relationship to a critical business application.
How does the Administrator use the Duplicate CI Remediator to resolve this issue?

options.text: Retain the manually imported CI, and delete the discovered CI
Merge the two CIs automatically, retaining all attributes from the discovered CI
Retain the discovered CI, but merge the relationship from the manually imported CI
Retain the discovered CI, and delete the manually imported CI

questions.explanation: The Duplicate CI Remediator allows you to merge CIs while selectively retaining attributes from each. The best approach here is to retain the discovered CI (which has the latest IP address) and merge the relationship from the manually imported CI (which has the critical business application connection). This preserves both the latest technical data and the important business relationship.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator wants to remove all Linux Servers in the organization that have not been updated in six months.
Which recommended action does the Administrator take in Data Manager?

options.text: Create a business rule
Create an archive policy
Create a scheduled job

questions.explanation: An archive policy in CMDB Data Manager is the recommended action for removing Linux servers that haven't been updated in six months. Archive policies automate the archival/deletion of stale CIs based on criteria like last update time. Business rules (A) are for custom scripting logic and not the recommended Data Manager approach. Scheduled jobs (C) alone don't provide the policy-driven governance that Data Manager offers.

questions.stem:
The CMDB Administrator group aims to display meaningful results on the CMDB Health Dashboard Compliance Scorecard for server records that are not on the latest patch.
What must be configured to achieve this goal?

options.text: Certification Policies, Data Filters, Scheduled Jobs
Stale, Orphan, Duplicate
Certification Filter, Certification Template, Audit
Technical Service Offerings, Dynamic CI Groups, CMDB Groups

questions.explanation: To display meaningful results on the CMDB Health Dashboard Compliance Scorecard for servers not on the latest patch, you need to configure a Certification Filter (to scope which CIs to evaluate), a Certification Template (to define what attributes to check), and an Audit (to actually run the compliance check). The Compliance scorecard is driven by audit results, so all three components must be configured.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator has been tasked with gathering information for a presentation to leadership. The Administrator needs to provide Duplicate CI, Orphan CI, and Stale CI metrics.
Which scorecard provides this information on the CMDB Health Dashboard?

options.text: Completeness
Compliance
Correctness

questions.explanation: The Correctness scorecard on the CMDB Health Dashboard provides metrics for Duplicate CIs, Orphan CIs, and Stale CIs. Correctness measures the accuracy of CI data through these three sub-metrics. Completeness (A) tracks required/recommended field population, and Compliance (B) is based on CMDB audit results. Only Correctness aggregates all three metrics requested.

questions.stem: What is the difference between Data Certification and Attestation policies when managing a CI?

options.text: Attestation requires correcting specific attributes of a CI, while Data Certification tracks acknowledgement the CI still exists.
Attestation can be scheduled, while Data Certification cannot be scheduled.
Attestation tracks acknowledgement the CI still exists, while Data Certification requires validating specific attributes of a CI.
Attestation can be assigned to a Group or an individual, while Data Certification can only be assigned to an individual.

questions.explanation: Attestation tracks acknowledgement that a CI still exists in the environment — it confirms CI existence. Data Certification requires validating specific attributes of a CI — it checks that data fields are accurate. Option A reverses these definitions. Certification and Attestation can both be scheduled (B is wrong). Both can be assigned to groups or individuals (D is wrong).

questions.stem: A CMDB Administrator is reviewing the health of the CMDB and notices a large percentage of the Hardware CIs are missing serial numbers. The Administrator is concerned this may cause duplicate CIs and would like to resolve the issue in a timely manner. What structured guidelines provided by ServiceNow are available to troubleshoot and resolve the issue?

options.text: CMDB Health Dashboards Playbooks
CSDM Now Create Playbooks
CSDB Data Foundations Dashboard Playbooks
CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard Playbooks

questions.explanation: The CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard provides Playbooks that guide administrators through improving CMDB health. The dashboard organizes maturity into stages (Foundation, Crawl, Walk, Run, Fly) and each stage has associated playbooks with specific actions and recommendations for improving data quality, coverage, and compliance.

questions.stem: Configuration Management needs to ensure data quality for all CIs in the CMDB. What areas of data quality for CIs are in the CMDB Health Dashboard? (Choose two.)

options.text: Missing CIs
State CIs
Duplicate CIs
Downgraded CIs
Upgraded CIs

questions.explanation: The CMDB Health Dashboard helps identify data quality issues including Missing CIs (gaps in discovery coverage where expected CIs are not in the CMDB) and Duplicate CIs (redundant records for the same physical or logical entity). These are tracked under the Correctness KPI. Stale Incidents and Expired Change Requests are ITSM concepts, not CMDB Health metrics.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Configuration Manager is reviewing the metrics on the CMDB Health Dashboard’s Correctness Scorecard for the Server class which consists of a total of 60,000 servers in the CMDB.
For the Duplicate metric, it shows Healthy CIs/Evaluated as 59,000/60,000.
For the Orphan metric, it shows Healthy CIs/Evaluated as 45,000/50,000.
Which configuration explains the difference in the scope of Server CIs (60,000 vs.50,000) evaluated between the two metrics?

options.text: The Duplicate metric has a CMDB Group configured for the Server class.
The Duplicate metric has a Health Inclusion rule configured for the Server class.
The Orphan metric has a Health Inclusion rule configured for the Server class.
The Orphan metric has a CMDB Group configured for the Server class.

questions.explanation: The difference in evaluated CIs between the Duplicate metric (60,000) and the Orphan metric (50,000) is because the Orphan metric has a Health Inclusion Rule configured for the Server class that limits its evaluation scope. Health Inclusion Rules define which CIs are included in specific health metric calculations. The Duplicate metric evaluates all 60,000 servers because it has no such filter, while the Orphan metric's inclusion rule excludes 10,000 servers.

questions.stem: CMDB class owners are receiving tasks under the ‘My Work’ tab in the CMDB Workspace. Which CMDB management tool is generating these tasks?

options.text: CMDB Data Manager
De-duplication templates
CMDB Health Dashboard

questions.explanation: CMDB Data Manager generates tasks under 'My Work' for class owners when data quality issues are detected. Through certification and attestation policies, Data Manager creates actionable tasks assigned to the responsible CI class owners, prompting them to review and correct data quality problems in their managed CI classes.

questions.stem: What ensures data volume in the CMDB manageable?

options.text: Scheduled Jobs
Archive Policies
Business Rules

questions.explanation: Archive Policies ensure data volume in the CMDB remains manageable by automatically archiving or deleting CIs that meet specified criteria (e.g., not updated within a time period). Scheduled Jobs (A) execute at intervals but don't inherently manage data volume. Business Rules (C) trigger on record operations but aren't designed for systematic data volume management.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Manager wants to improve data quality using the CMDB Health Dashboard.
What needs to happen to generate CMDB health scores?

options.text: Nothing, CMDB health scores are calculated by default
The plugin, CMDB health calculation, needs to be installed
The scheduled jobs for the CMDB Health Dashboard must be activated

questions.explanation: To generate CMDB health scores, the scheduled jobs for the CMDB Health Dashboard must be activated. These jobs calculate the health metrics (Correctness, Compliance, Completeness) on a recurring basis. Health scores are not calculated by default (A is wrong) — the scheduled jobs must be manually enabled. There is no separate 'CMDB health calculation' plugin (B is incorrect) as the functionality is part of the core CMDB.

questions.stem:
The CMDB Configuration Manager is using the CI Class Manager to manage the group ownership of CI classes and needs to leverage the ownership value specified in the CI Class Manager.
When configuring a CMDB Data Manager policy, which group reference field should be set?

options.text: Change Group
Approval Group
Managed By Group
Support Group

questions.explanation: The 'Managed By Group' reference field in CI Class Manager specifies the group ownership for CI classes. When configuring a CMDB Data Manager policy, setting the group reference to 'Managed By Group' leverages the ownership value from CI Class Manager. This ensures policy tasks are assigned to the correct group. Change Group (A), Approval Group (B), and Support Group (D) serve different operational purposes.

questions.stem:
The CMDB Configuration Management team wants to manage de-duplication tasks generated from data ingested into the CMDB via the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE).
In which area of the CMDB Workspace can they locate these de-duplication tasks?

options.text: Important actions tile under the Home tab
CMDB feature adoption tile under the Insight tab
Total status tile under the My Work tab

questions.explanation: De-duplication tasks generated from the IRE can be located in the Total status tile under the My Work tab of the CMDB Workspace. This tab shows all assigned tasks including de-duplication remediation tasks. The Important actions tile on the Home tab (A) shows high-level alerts, and the CMDB feature adoption tile on the Insight tab (B) tracks feature usage rather than individual tasks.

questions.stem: Which type of CMDB Data Manager policy creates tasks that allow the assigned individual to update fields on the CI record?

options.text: Compliance
Certification
Attestation
Audit

questions.explanation: The Certification policy type in CMDB Data Manager creates tasks that allow assigned individuals to update and validate specific fields on CI records. Certification policies define which attributes need verification and generate tasks for the assigned person to review and update those fields. Attestation (C) validates whether a CI still exists. Compliance (A) and Audit (D) are related to health scoring, not field update tasks.

questions.stem:
DRAG DROP -
A new ServiceNow customer is assembling a Configuration Management team to support their CMDB.
Drag each role to its corresponding job description.
questions.explanation: Configuration Management team roles include: Configuration Manager (overall CMDB strategy and governance), Configuration Analyst (day-to-day CMDB data quality and remediation), CI Class Owner/Manager (manages specific CI classes and their health), and Process Owner (defines processes around CMDB data management). Each role has distinct responsibilities in maintaining CMDB integrity.

questions.stem:
DRAG DROP -
A CMDB Administrator seeks to understand the available tools for preventing, addressing, and remediating duplicate CIs.
Drag and drop each feature with the corresponding outcome.
Some options may not apply.
questions.explanation: Tools for preventing and remediating duplicate CIs include: Identification Rules (prevent duplicates by matching CIs on criterion attributes during import), De-duplication Tasks (generate tasks to merge identified duplicates), Duplicate CI Remediator (merge duplicate CIs while retaining important attributes and relationships), and Independent IRE (processes data through identification before insertion).

questions.stem:
A Configuration Manager needs to leverage a policy type to automate the creation and assignment of tasks to validate the existence of CIs.
Which policy type should be used to accomplish this goal?

options.text: Retire
Certification
Delete
Attestation

questions.explanation: The Attestation policy type automates the creation and assignment of tasks to validate the existence of CIs. Attestation asks assignees to confirm whether a CI still exists in the environment. Certification (B) validates specific CI attributes rather than existence. Retire (A) and Delete (C) are lifecycle actions for removing CIs, not for validating their existence.

questions.stem: Which is a purpose or requirement of CMDB Data Manager in ServiceNow?

options.text: Encrypts archived records for enhanced security
Automates the enforcement of relationship rules between CIs in the CMDB
Automates the archival and deletion of records based on retention policies

questions.explanation: CMDB Data Manager automates the archival and deletion of records based on retention policies. It provides governance over the CI lifecycle through policy types including certification, attestation, archival, and retirement. It does not encrypt archived records (A) and its primary purpose is not enforcing relationship rules (B) — that's handled by the IRE and relationship rules.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Data Manager needs to access the ServiceNow platform to create, publish, and manage policies that automate and govern CI lifecycle operations, ensuring the CMDB remains healthy and efficient.
Where can the Data Manager do this?

options.text: CMDB Workspace Management tab
Service Operations Workspace
CMDB Workspace CMDB 360 tab
CI Class Manager

questions.explanation: The CMDB Data Manager is accessed from the CMDB Workspace Management tab. The Management section includes CMDB management tools organized in categories including an Optimize section where Data Manager policies can be created, published, and managed. Service Operations Workspace (B) is for ITOM, the CMDB 360 tab (C) is for multisource views, and CI Class Manager (D) manages class definitions.

questions.stem:
DRAG DROP -
A manufacturing organization has implemented Incident Management in ServiceNow and wants to integrate additional products to enhance its functionality.
Drag each ServiceNow product to the value it brings to supporting Incident Management.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow products supporting Incident Management: Discovery (provides accurate CI data for faster root cause analysis), Service Mapping (maps application service dependencies for impact analysis), Event Management (correlates events to incidents for automated response), and CMDB (provides the foundation of CI relationships for understanding service impact during incidents).

questions.stem: Where can a CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB Saved Query be viewed and created in the CMDB Workspace?

options.text: Saved queries window on the Insight tab
CMDB Query Builder
Coverage window on the CMDB 360 tab
Saved queries window on the CMDB 360 tab

questions.explanation: CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB Saved Queries can be viewed and created in the Saved queries window on the CMDB 360 tab within CMDB Workspace. This tab provides the CMDB 360 view with coverage information, saved queries, and reconciliation details. The Insight tab (A) shows analytics, the CMDB Query Builder (B) is separate, and the Coverage window (C) shows source coverage but not saved queries.

questions.stem:
An organization is changing data centers and needs to know the consequences of the planned changes.
How can Application Service mapping be used as part of Change Management?

options.text: To understand the physical location of CIs
To identify which devices will go offline first
To understand the business impact of CIs

questions.explanation: Application Service mapping provides visibility into CI dependencies and their connection to business services. For Change Management, this enables understanding the business impact of CIs — knowing which business services are affected when specific CIs undergo changes. Physical location (A) is tracked by CI attributes, not service mapping. Device offline order (B) is operational planning, not service mapping's primary value.

questions.stem: Where can an administrator perform Natural Language Queries (NLQ)?

options.text: CMDB Data Manager
CI Class Manager
CMDB Workspace
CMDB Health Dashboard

questions.explanation: Natural Language Queries (NLQ) can be performed in the CMDB Workspace. The workspace provides an interface where administrators can type natural language questions to query CMDB data. CMDB Data Manager (A) handles policies, CI Class Manager (B) manages class hierarchy, and CMDB Health Dashboard (D) displays health metrics, but NLQ functionality is specifically in CMDB Workspace.

questions.stem:
A healthcare provider faces a critical incident affecting its patient management system. The provider needs to determine the users impacted to mitigate disruption effectively.
Which CSDM-related data should they leverage?

options.text: Incident history of similar CIs
Application Service environment attribute
Service Offerings by Department or Location
Affected CI [task_ci] related list

questions.explanation: Service Offerings by Department or Location provides CSDM-related data to determine impacted users during an incident. By understanding which service offerings serve which departments and locations, the provider can identify which user groups are affected when the patient management system goes down. Incident history (A) shows past patterns, not current user impact. Application Service environment (B) shows environment type, not user impact.

questions.stem:
A Configuration Manager wants to use the Unified Map.
Where would it be accessed?

options.text: CMDB Data Manager
CI Class Manager
CMDB Workspace

questions.explanation: The Unified Map is accessed from within the CMDB Workspace. It provides a visual representation of CI relationships and service compositions. CMDB Data Manager (A) manages CI lifecycle policies and CI Class Manager (B) manages class definitions — neither provides map visualization. The CMDB Workspace is the central hub for CMDB visualization and management.

questions.stem:
A service owner is using Unified Map to understand to composition of a service but wants to filter out irrelevant information.
Which options are available to the service owner from the filter panel? (Choose two.)

options.text: Discovery source
CI type
Business critically
Managed by group

questions.explanation: The Unified Map filter panel offers filtering by Discovery source (A) to show only CIs from specific discovery methods, and CI type (B) to filter by CI class. These are the standard filter options for narrowing down the service composition view. Business criticality (C) and Managed by group (D) are CI attributes but are not available as Unified Map filter panel options.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator wants to create a CMDB query to find all databases located in Seattle that are connected to application services. They also want to include incidents related to those databases.
Which actions does the company take to build this query? (Choose two.)

options.text: Add to the canvas the Incident table from the Non-CMDB Tables list
Add a filter to the database node for location=Seattle
Set the relationship level to ‘Up to 2nd level relationships’
Add property columns to the application service node

questions.explanation: To build a CMDB query finding databases in Seattle connected to application services with related incidents: (A) add the Incident table from the Non-CMDB Tables list (since incidents aren't CMDB CIs), and (B) add a filter to the database node for location=Seattle. Setting relationship level (C) and adding property columns (D) are optional display settings, not essential actions for building the query.

questions.stem:
In a company there is a need to understand the CSDM maturity level needed. Different stakeholders listed a number of use cases that they expect over time.
Which use case requires information objects?

options.text: The Event Operations team wants to automate their events into incident for operational actions.
The Business Service Management team wants to understand the operational impact for their consumer parties.
The Customer Service team wants to onboard pro-active case management.
The SecOps team wants to understand the operational risk in the Business Application context.
The Asset Management wants to understand to asset life cycle compliancy in a Business Application context.

questions.explanation: The SecOps team wanting to understand operational risk in the Business Application context requires Information Objects. Information Objects in CSDM represent data entities (databases, data stores) that applications handle. Understanding which sensitive data/information objects a business application processes is essential for assessing security and operational risk. The other use cases involve infrastructure CIs, service relationships, or asset lifecycle — not information objects.

questions.stem:
A Platform Owner is collaborating with stakeholders in the manufacturing industry to align their CIs with the CSDM 5 framework. They need to map production line monitoring systems to the appropriate CSDM domain.
Which CSDM 5 domain does the Platform Owner use?

options.text: Build and Integration (Build)
Service Delivery (Manage Technical)
Service Consumption (Sell/Consume)
Design and Planning (Design)
Foundation

questions.explanation: Production line monitoring systems in manufacturing should be mapped to the Service Delivery (Manage Technical) domain in CSDM 5. This domain covers operational infrastructure, monitoring systems, and technical services that support business operations. Foundation (E) covers base data like locations and departments. Design (D) is for architecture and standards. Build (A) is for development/integration. Service Consumption (C) is for customer-facing services.

questions.stem:
A development team is working on a project and an application will be deployed to many servers. There will be several security requirements that must be checked to adhere to lawful compliance because the application will be holding customer personal data (PII and PCI).
Where in the CSDM does the development team look to store the information that will be used to satisfy the audits?

options.text: Technology Management Service Offerings (Technical Service Offerings) and Dynamic CI Groups
Business Applications and Information Objects
Customer Service Offerings and Databases

questions.explanation: Business Applications and Information Objects is where the development team stores information for security audits. Business Applications represent the deployed application, while Information Objects represent the data (PII and PCI) the application handles. Together they provide the context needed for compliance audits around customer personal data. Technical Service Offerings (A) lack the data classification aspect. Customer Service Offerings (C) are customer-facing.

questions.stem:
A customer’s CMDB is aligned to the CSDM Walk stage.
What benefit is provided by the CMDB?

options.text: Enables impact assessments for incident, problem, and change on Business Services
Improves the implementation velocity of APM Foundation for future business application rationalization
Allows for additional stratification of Technical team’s support structure along the lines of OLAs and commitments

questions.explanation: At the CSDM Walk stage, the CMDB enables impact assessments for incident, problem, and change on Business Services. The Walk stage establishes service-aware relationships between infrastructure CIs, applications, and business services, making it possible to understand how changes or incidents to CIs affect the business. APM Foundation (B) is more relevant at advanced stages. OLA stratification (C) is not a primary Walk stage benefit.

questions.stem:
DRAG DROP -
Some steps need to be taken to transition from using different status attributes in the CMDB to life cycle objects.
Drag and drop the objectives/attributes to the description.
questions.explanation: Transitioning from legacy CMDB status fields to CSDM life cycle objects involves: defining Life Cycle Stages (the lifecycle phases like Production, Retired), mapping Life Cycle Stage Statuses (specific statuses within each stage), creating Life Cycle Mappings (mapping from legacy status field values to CSDM stages), and configuring Life Cycle Controls (governing allowed transitions).

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator wants to improve data quality related to the CSDM.
Which action should the Administrator take to meet this goal?

options.text: Use the default configured CMDB Health Dashboard
Start the ServiceNow Health Scan
Use the CSDM Data Foundation Dashboard

questions.explanation: The CSDM Data Foundation Dashboard is specifically designed to improve data quality related to CSDM. It provides metrics for each CSDM maturity stage (Foundation, Crawl, Walk, Run, Fly) with Get Well Playbooks for remediation. The default CMDB Health Dashboard (A) tracks general CMDB health, not CSDM-specific quality. ServiceNow Health Scan (B) is for platform health checks, not CSDM data quality.

questions.stem:
According to the Common Service Data Model (CSDM), a server team is requesting a catalog item be created for infrastructure upgrade requests.
Which role is involved in initiating the request and defining requirements?

options.text: Enterprise Architecture
Technology Service Owners
Application Service Owners

questions.explanation: Technology Service Owners are responsible for initiating infrastructure upgrade requests and defining requirements in the CSDM context. Since a server team is requesting infrastructure upgrades, they fall under the Technology Services domain. Enterprise Architecture (A) focuses on strategy and standards. Application Service Owners (C) manage application-level services, not infrastructure hardware.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator is evaluating whether to monitor the metrics provided on the CMDB Foundation Dashboard.
Which benefits support the decision to continually monitor the results on this dashboard? (Choose two.)

options.text: Provides a list of all CIs that failed health audits
Provides metrics for CIs Processed by the IRE
Provides metrics on active CIs updated in the last 90 days
Reports on all orphan CIs in the CMDB

questions.explanation: The CMDB Foundation Dashboard benefits that support continual monitoring include: (B) providing metrics for CIs Processed by the IRE, which tracks data ingestion quality, and (C) providing metrics on active CIs updated in the last 90 days, which monitors data freshness. It does not provide detailed lists of CIs that failed health audits (A) nor comprehensive orphan CI reports (D) — those are CMDB Health Dashboard features.

questions.stem:
The Configuration Manager is preparing the justification to utilize the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard.
Which benefits align with the usage of this dashboard? (Choose two.)

options.text: It enables monitoring and tracking of CMDB health over time.
It provides actionable insights to improve data quality and completeness.
It helps detect and eliminate duplicate records in the CMD
It automates the approval process for change management.

questions.explanation: The CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard enables (A) monitoring and tracking of CMDB health over time with trend metrics, and (B) provides actionable insights through Get Well Playbooks to improve data quality and completeness. Detecting and eliminating duplicates (C) is handled by the de-duplication tools and Health Dashboard, not the Data Foundations Dashboard. Automating change approval (D) is unrelated.

questions.stem:
A Change Manager wants to gain value from CSDM.
How will the Change Management process benefit from CSDM? (Choose two.)

options.text: Identify blackout windows for the change
Determine the root cause of the change issue
Understand the impact of the change on services
Route the change dynamically

questions.explanation: Change Management benefits from CSDM by: (C) understanding the impact of changes on services through mapped CI-to-service relationships, and (D) routing changes dynamically based on CMDB data like CI ownership (Managed By Group). Identifying blackout windows (A) is a scheduling feature, not directly from CSDM. Root cause determination (B) is a Problem Management activity, not Change Management.

questions.stem: Which are business values of CMDB? (Choose two.)

options.text: Collecting and managing financial data
Streaming incident and change management
Strengthening operational resiliency
Automating maintenance for CI relationships

questions.explanation: Business values of CMDB include: (B) streamlining incident and change management by providing accurate CI relationships and service dependencies, and (C) strengthening operational resiliency by enabling impact analysis and proactive management. Collecting financial data (A) is financial management's domain, not a core CMDB business value. Automating CI relationship maintenance (D) is a feature, not a business outcome value.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator is implementing a Vulnerability Response or Security Incident Response and needs to ensure customers have enough context to estimate risk and set task priorities.
Which Get Well Playbook from the CSDM Data Foundation Dashboard helps with this?

options.text: Locations without a Parent Location
Named Product Models without Product Owners
Percentage of Custom Status Values for CI Life Cycle Stages
Application Services with Business Application Relationships

questions.explanation: The 'Application Services with Business Application Relationships' Get Well Playbook helps ensure customers have context to estimate risk and set task priorities for Vulnerability Response and Security Incident Response. When application services have proper business application relationships, security teams can understand which business applications are at risk, enabling proper prioritization of remediation tasks.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator wants to run the Services Have Owners Identified playbook to remediate the issues shown in the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard.
Which remediation plays would be used? (Choose two.)

options.text: Govern Data
Fix Data
Report Data
Analyze Data

questions.explanation: The 'Services Have Owners Identified' playbook uses (B) Fix Data plays to remediate the data by assigning owners to services, and (D) Analyze Data plays to first identify which services lack owners. The playbook workflow analyzes the current state of service ownership data and then provides actions to fix it. Govern Data (A) and Report Data (C) are different play types not central to this specific remediation.

questions.stem:
A Configuration Management Governance team is transitioning from utilizing legacy CMDB status fields to CSDM life cycle status fields.
Which table can be modified?

options.text: Life Cycle Stages [life_cycle_stage]
Life Cycle Mapping [life_cycle_mapping]
Life Cycle Controls [life_cycle_control]
Life Cycle Stage Status [life_cycle_stage_status]

questions.explanation: The Life Cycle Stage Status [life_cycle_stage_status] table contains the specific status values within each life cycle stage and can be modified when transitioning from legacy status fields. This table defines statuses like 'Active', 'Planned', 'Retired' within stages. Life Cycle Stages (A) defines the stages themselves. Life Cycle Mapping (B) maps legacy values. Life Cycle Controls (C) governs allowed transitions.

questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator, viewing the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard, notices the Unique Locations Result percentage low.
What is the recommended process from the associated playbook to correct this issue?

options.text: Review both locations, update CIs with the correct location and delete the duplicate location
Retain the location that matches the organization’s standard naming convention, and delete the duplicate without further validation
Keep both locations as either can be used as a valid alternate location
Use the Duplicate CI Remediator the merge the duplicate location records

questions.explanation: The recommended process from the associated playbook for low Unique Locations percentage is to review both duplicate/similar locations, update CIs with the correct location, and then delete the duplicate location. This ensures CIs reference the standardized location record. Simply retaining the matching naming convention (B) skips validation. Keeping both locations (C) doesn't resolve the issue. Using Duplicate CI Remediator (D) is for CIs, not locations.

questions.stem:
DRAG DROP -
A CMDB Owner starts on the CSDM journey and needs to become familiar with the CSDM domains.
Drag the CMDB objects to the correct CSDM domains.
questions.explanation: CSDM domains organize CMDB objects: Foundation (locations, departments, users, groups, companies), Design (business capabilities, information objects, technology standards), Manage Technical (application services, technical services, CIs, clusters), and Sell/Consume (service offerings, subscriptions, entitlements). Each domain serves a distinct purpose in the service data model.

questions.stem:
A Configuration Manager is planning the implementation of the CMDB.
Which is the prescribed CSDM rollout order?

options.text: Architecture, Business, Technical, Governance
Initiate, Plan, Execute, Deliver, Close
Foundation, Crawl, Walk, Run, Fly
Initial, Developing, Defined, Managed

questions.explanation: The prescribed CSDM rollout order is Foundation, Crawl, Walk, Run, Fly. Foundation establishes base data (locations, departments), Crawl implements ITSM-related CMDB tables, Walk adds network infrastructure and applications, Run builds technology-to-business relationships, and Fly represents full CSDM maturity. This is the sequential implementation framework ServiceNow prescribes for CSDM adoption.

questions.stem:
A retail company has a generative AI (GenAI) product recommendation application that uses Amazon Bedrock. The application suggests products to customers based on browsing history and demographics. The company needs to implement fairness evaluation across multiple demographic groups to detect and measure bias in recommendations between two prompt approaches. The company wants to collect and monitor fairness metrics in real time. The company must receive an alert if the fairness metrics show a discrepancy of more than 15% between demographic groups. The company must receive weekly reports that compare the performance of the two prompt approaches.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST custom development effort?

options.text: Configure an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard to display default metrics from Amazon Bedrock API calls. Create custom metrics based on model outputs. Set up Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke AWS lambda functions that perform post-processing analysis on model responses and publish custom fairness metrics.

Create the two prompt variants in Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management. Use Amazon Bedrock Flows to deploy the prompt variants with defined traffic allocation. Configure Amazon Bedrock guardrails that have content filters to monitor demographic fairness. Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms on the GuardrailContentSource dimension that use InvocationsIntervened metrics to detect recommendation discrepancy threshold violations.

Set up Amazon SageMaker Clarify to analyze model outputs. Publish fairness metrics to Amazon CloudWatch. Create CloudWatch composite alarms that combine SageMaker Clarify bias metrics with Amazon Bedrock latency metrics to provide a comprehensive fairness evaluation dashboard.

Create an Amazon Bedrock model evaluation job to compare fairness between the two prompt variants. Enable model invocation logging in Amazon CloudWatch. Set up CloudWatch alarms for InvocationsIntervened metrics with a dimension for each demographic group.

questions.stem:
A finance company is developing an AI assistant to help clients plan investments and manage their portfolios. The company identifies several high-risk conversation patterns such as requests for specific stock recommendations or guaranteed returns. High-risk conversation patterns could lead to regulatory violations if the company cannot implement appropriate controls.
The company must ensure that the AI assistant does not provide inappropriate financial advice, generate content about competitors, or make claims that are not factually grounded in the company's approved financial guidance. The company wants to use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to implement a solution.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Add the high-risk conversation patterns to a denied topics guardrail.
Configure a content filter guardrail to filter prompts that contain the high-risk conversation patterns.
Configure a content filter guardrail to filter prompts that contain competitor names.
Add the names of competitors as custom word filters. Set the input and output actions to block.
Set a low grounding score threshold.
Set a high grounding score threshold.

questions.stem:
A company has deployed an AI assistant as a React application that uses AWS Amplify, an AWS AppSync GraphQL API, and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. The application uses the GraphQL API to call the Amazon Bedrock RetrieveAndGenerate API for knowledge base interactions. The company configures an AWS Lambda resolver to use the RequestResponse invocation type.
Application users report frequent timeouts and slow response times. Users report these problems more frequently for complex questions that require longer processing.
The company needs a solution to fix these performance issues and enhance the user experience.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Amplify AI Kit to implement streaming responses from the GraphQL API and to optimize client-side rendering.
Increase the timeout value of the Lambda resolver. Implement retry logic with exponential backoff.
Update the application to send an API request to an Amazon SQS queue. Update the AWS AppSync resolver to poll and process the queue.
Change the RetrieveAndGenerate API to the InvokeModelWithResponseStream API. Update the application to use an Amazon API Gateway WebSocket API to support the streaming response.

questions.stem:
An ecommerce company operates a global product recommendation system that needs to switch between multiple foundation models (FM) in Amazon Bedrock based on regulations, cost optimization, and performance requirements. The company must apply custom controls based on proprietary business logic, including dynamic cost thresholds, AWS Region-specific compliance rules, and real-time A/B testing across multiple FMs. The system must be able to switch between FMs without deploying new code. The system must route user requests based on complex rules including user tier, transaction value, regulatory zone, and real-time cost metrics that change hourly and require immediate propagation across thousands of concurrent requests.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Deploy an AWS Lambda function that uses environment variables to store routing rules and Amazon Bedrock FM IDs. Use the Lambda console to update the environment variables when business requirements change. Configure an Amazon API Gateway REST API to read request parameters to make routing decisions.

Deploy Amazon API Gateway REST API request transformation templates to implement routing logic based on request attributes. Store Amazon Bedrock FM endpoints as REST API stage variables. Update the variables when the system switches between models.

Configure an AWS Lambda function to fetch routing configurations from the AWS AppConfig Agent for each user request. Run business logic in the Lambda function to select the appropriate FM for each request. Expose the FM through a single Amazon API Gateway REST API endpoint.

Use AWS Lambda authorizers for an Amazon API Gateway REST API to evaluate routing rules that are stored in AWS AppConfig. Return authorization contexts based on business logic. Route requests to model-specific Lambda functions for each Amazon Bedrock FM.

questions.stem:
A company is developing an internal generative AI (GenAI) assistant that uses Amazon Bedrock to summarize corporate documents for multiple business units. The GenAI assistant must generate responses in a consistent format that includes a document summary, classification of business risks, and terms that are flagged for review. The GenAI assistant must adapt the tone of responses for each user's business unit, such as legal, human resources, or finance. The GenAI assistant must block hate speech, inappropriate topics, and sensitive information such as personal health information.
The company needs a solution to centrally manage prompt variants across business units and teams. The company wants to minimize ongoing orchestration efforts and maintenance for post-processing logic. The company also wants to have the ability to adjust content moderation criteria for the GenAI assistant over time.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST maintenance overhead?

options.text: Use Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management to configure reusable templates and business unit-specific prompt variants. Apply Amazon Bedrock guardrails that have category filters and sensitive term lists to block prohibited content.

Use Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management to define base templates. Enforce business unit-specific tone by using system prompt variables. Configure Amazon Bedrock guardrails to apply audience-based threshold tuning. Manage the guardrails by using an internal administration API.
Use Amazon Bedrock with business unit-based instruction injection in API calls. Store response formatting rules in Amazon DynamoD
Use AWS Step functions to validate responses. Use Amazon Comprehend to apply content filters after the GenAI assistant generates responses.
Use Amazon Bedrock with custom prompt templates that are stored in Amazon DynamoD
Create one AWS Lambda function to select business unit-specific prompts. Create a second Lambda function to call Amazon Comprehend to filter prohibited content from responses.

questions.stem:
A financial services company is building a customer support application that retrieves relevant financial regulation documents from a database based on semantic similarities to user queries. The application must integrate with Amazon Bedrock to generate responses. The application must be able to search documents that are in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. The application must filter documents by metadata such as publication date, regulatory agency, and document type.
The database stores approximately 10 million document embeddings. To minimize operational overhead, the company wants a solution that minimizes management and maintenance effort. The application must provide low-latency responses for real-time customer interactions.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon OpenSearch Serverless to provide vector search capabilities and metadata filtering. Connect to Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases to enable Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) capabilities that use an Anthropic Claude foundation model (FM).

Deploy an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database with the pgvector extension. Define tables to store embeddings and metadata. Use SQL queries to perform similarity searches. Send retrieved documents to Amazon Bedrock to generate responses.
Use Amazon S3 Vectors to configure a vector index and non-filterable metadata fields. Integrate S3 Vectors with Amazon Bedrock to enable Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) capabilities.

Set up an Amazon Neptune Analytics graph database. Configure a vector index that has appropriate dimensionality to store document embeddings. Use Amazon Bedrock to perform graph-based retrieval and to generate responses.

questions.stem:
A medical company is building a generative AI (GenAI) application that uses RAG to provide evidence-based medical information. The application uses Amazon OpenSearch Service to retrieve vector embeddings. Users report that searches frequently miss results that contain exact medical terms and acronyms and return too many semantically similar but irrelevant documents. The company needs to improve retrieval quality and maintain low end user latency, even as the document collection grows to millions of documents.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Configure hybrid search by combining vector similarity with keyword matching to improve semantic understanding and exact term and acronym matching.
Increase the dimensions of the vector embeddings from 384 to 1536. Use a post-processing AWS Lambda function to filter out irrelevant results after retrieval.
Replace OpenSearch Service with Amazon Kendra. Use query expansion to handle medical acronyms and terminology variants during pre-processing.
Implement a two-stage retrieval architecture in which initial vector search results are re-ranked by an ML model that is hosted on Amazon SageMaker AI.

questions.stem:
A company runs a generative AI (GenAI)-powered summarization application in an application AWS account that uses Amazon Bedrock. The application architecture includes an Amazon API Gateway REST API that forwards requests to AWS Lambda functions that are attached to private VPC subnets. The application summarizes sensitive customer records that the company stores in a governed data lake in a centralized data storage account. The company has enabled Amazon S3, Amazon Athena, and AWS Glue in the data storage account.
The company must ensure that calls that the application makes to Amazon Bedrock use only private connectivity between the company's application VPC and Amazon Bedrock. The company's data lake must provide fine-grained column-level access across the company's AWS accounts.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: In the application account, create interface VPC endpoints for Amazon Bedrock runtimes. Run Lambda functions in private subnets. Use IAM conditions on inference and data-plane policies to allow calls only to approved endpoints and roles. In the data storage account, use AWS Lake Formation LF-tag-based access control to create table and column-level cross-account grants.

Run Lambda functions in private subnets. Configure a NAT gateway to provide access to Amazon Bedrock and the data lake. Use S3 bucket policies and ACLs to manage permissions. Export AWS CloudTrail logs to Amazon S3 to perform weekly reviews.

Create a gateway endpoint only for Amazon S3 in the application account. Invoke Amazon Bedrock through public endpoints. Use database-level grants in AWS Lake Formation to manage data access. Stream AWS CloudTrail logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Do not set up metric filters or alarms.

Use VPC endpoints to provide access to Amazon Bedrock and Amazon S3 in the application account. Use only IAM path-based policies to manage data lake access. Send AWS CloudTrail logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Periodically create dashboards and allow public fallback for cross-Region reads to reduce setup time.

questions.stem:
A media company must use Amazon Bedrock to implement a robust governance process for AI-generated content. The company needs to manage hundreds of prompt templates. Multiple teams use the templates across multiple AWS Regions to generate content. The solution must provide version control with approval workflows that include notifications for pending reviews. The solution must also provide detailed audit trails that document prompt activities and consistent prompt parameterization to enforce quality standards.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure Amazon Bedrock Studio prompt templates. Use Amazon CloudWatch to create dashboards that display prompt usage metrics. Store the approval status of content in Amazon DynamoD
Use AWS Lambda functions to enforce approvals.

Use Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management to implement version control. Configure AWS CloudTrail for audit logging. Use IAM policies to control approval permissions. Create parameterized prompt templates by specifying variables.
Use AWS Step Functions to create an approval workflow. Store prompts as documents in Amazon S3. Use tags to implement version control. Use Amazon EventBridge to send notifications.
Deploy Amazon SageMaker Canvas with prompt templates that are stored in Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudFormation to implement version control. Use AWS Config to enforce approval policies.

questions.stem:
A company is developing a customer support application that uses Amazon Bedrock foundation models (FMs) to provide real-time AI assistance to the company's employees. The application must display AI-generated responses character by character as the responses are generated. The application needs to support thousands of concurrent users with minimal latency. The responses typically take 15 to 45 seconds to finish.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure an Amazon API Gateway WebSocket API with an AWS Lambda integration. Configure the WebSocket API to invoke the Amazon Bedrock InvokeModelWithResponseStream API and stream partial responses through WebSocket connections.

Configure an Amazon API Gateway REST API with an AWS Lambda integration. Configure the REST API to invoke the Amazon Bedrock standard InvokeModel API and implement frontend client-side polling every 100 ms for complete response chunks.
Implement direct frontend client connections to Amazon Bedrock by using IAM user credentials and the InvokeModelWithResponseStream API without any intermediate gateway or proxy layer.

Configure an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API with an AWS Lambda integration. Configure the HTTP API to cache complete responses in an Amazon DynamoDB table and serve the responses through multiple paginated GET requests to frontend clients.

questions.stem:
A company is using Amazon Bedrock to design an application to help researchers apply for grants. The application is based on an Amazon Nova Pro foundation model (FM). The application contains four required inputs and must provide responses in a consistent text format. The company wants to receive a notification in Amazon Bedrock if a response contains bullying language. However, the company does not want to block all flagged responses.
The company creates an Amazon Bedrock flow that takes an input prompt and sends it to the Amazon Nova Pro FM. The Amazon Nova Pro FM provides a response.
Which additional steps must the company take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management to specify the required inputs as variables. Select an Amazon Nova Pro FM. Specify the output format for the response. Add the prompt to the prompts node of the flow.
Create an Amazon Bedrock guardrail that applies the hate content filter. Set the filter response to block. Add the guardrail to the prompts node of the flow.

Create an Amazon Bedrock prompt router. Specify an Amazon Nova Pro FM. Add the required inputs as variables to the input node of the flow. Add the prompt router to the prompts node. Add the output format to the output node.
